item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Sep 26, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Aladdin Jr — Sat Sep 26, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
Based on the iconic animated film, with an Academy Award-winning score by Alan Menken, Howard Ashman and Tim Rice, Disney’s Aladdin Jr. is sure to send audiences soaring on a flying carpet ride filled with romance and adventure. When the street urchin, Aladdin, vies for the attention of the beautiful princess, Jasmine, he uses a genie’s magic power to become a prince in order to marry her. Iago, Jafar, the Genie and more are here in Disney’s Aladdin JR., a musical adventure filled with magic, mayhem and the power of love. Recommended for all ages

item.title: Film: The Palestine Exception — Sat Sep 26, 4:00 PM — Cruess Hall
item.description:
You are invited to a special screening and discussion as part of the Davis Palestine Film Series. We will be showing the documentary “The Palestine Exception,” followed by a panel and conversation. About the Film: Described as a “searing and unflinchingly honest account of what it means to stand for something,” this documentary explores the immense consequences of speaking up against injustice. It offers a vital look at how institutional power attempts to enforce silence on its critics, a theme that feels particularly urgent for our present moment. Event Details: Date: Saturday, September 26 Time: 4:00 PM – 6:30 PM (please give yourself extra time to travel and park your car or bike; programming will begin promptly at 4:00) Location: UC Davis Cruess Hall Theater Address: 375 California Ave, Davis Parking: Easy & FREE parking available on-site on campus, just across from Cruess Hall
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Sat Sep 26, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up

item.title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis) — Sun Oct 25, 1:00 PM — Blanchard Room
item.description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States.
The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.
The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.
Source: Yolo Library

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Dec 24, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Sep 26, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p

item.title: Shields Library Mural Dedication — Fri Oct 2, 1:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
join us in celebrating our new library mural, created by undergraduate students in the Mural Workshop (ART 171/CHI 171) in Spring 2026. Drawing on the Chicanx tradition of muralism, the students' creative process centered on community engagement, collective storytelling, and sense of place. Vibrant imagery of students, photos from the library's University Archives, and an oak tree bearing the words “Saber es Poder” (“Knowledge is Power”) are among the elements that explore the library as a space where preservation and empowerment meet. Learn more about the mural.
Meet some of the artists who created the mural and see footage of the making of this beautiful work of art. Light refreshments available while they last. Free and open to all.
Source: UC Davis Library

item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 17, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

Join bestselling author, actor, activist, and beloved storyteller Tyler Merritt for a one-of-a-kind live experience filled with unforgettable stories, humor, music, heartfelt conversation, and practical encouragement. item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Fri Sep 25, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Hunter, Bran, & Brown Live — Fri Sep 25, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Join Laurin Hunter, Brandon “someguyBran” Dominguez and David J. Brown for an evening of original music, storytelling and collaboration. Blending influences that span jazz, folk, Americana, pop, rock, soul and beyond, each artist brings a distinct musical voice while sharing a passion for authentic live performance. Together, they’ll present an evening of original songs, fresh interpretations of timeless classics, creativity and connection where every performance offers something unique.
Source: The Dirt
